meta.title: Certification Learning Roadmap
meta.owner: Thabo Pali — Systems Integration Engineer & Full-Stack Developer
meta.subtitle: Objectives, concepts, and prerequisite basics, organized by priority — Year 1 core five, then conditional/optional additions.
meta.metaNote: Content reflects official exam guides as of August 2026. AI-200, AI-103, and ITIL Foundation (Version 5) are all newly current — check learn.microsoft.com/credentials and peoplecert.org before registering, since this landscape has shifted twice already since this roadmap was first drafted (AZ-204 retired, ITIL moved to v5). Checked items save in this browser via local storage — they'll still be here next time you open this link on this device, but won't follow you to a different browser or computer. Content itself lives in data/roadmap.json — edit that file and redeploy to update anything on this page.

foundational.heading: Foundational basics worth shoring up before you start

items.title: Python fluency.
items.body: Both AI-200 and AI-103 explicitly list Python proficiency as a prerequisite — your Django/FastAPI background covers the syntax, but review Azure SDK usage patterns specifically (the `azure-*` Python SDK family), since exam scenarios are SDK-call-based, not general scripting.

items.title: Docker / containers.
items.body: AI-200's first domain and all of CKA (plus CKAD, if you go there) assume solid container fundamentals. No separate cert needed — but build genuine hands-on comfort: images, Dockerfiles, registries, basic Compose.

items.title: YAML fluency.
items.body: Terraform (HCL is YAML-adjacent) and Kubernetes manifests are both YAML/declarative-config-heavy. If you're mostly used to C#/JSON-style config, budget a few hours purely on reading and writing YAML confidently.

items.title: Linux command line.
items.body: CKA and CKAD are both 100% terminal-based with no GUI fallback. Your SharePoint/Windows-server background is real infrastructure experience, but spend deliberate time in a Linux shell (bash, systemctl basics, file permissions) if that's not already daily habit.

year1.title: ITIL Foundation (Version 5)
year1.issuer: PeopleCert / AXELOS — current edition, supersedes ITIL 4
year1.estTime: Est. 2–3 weeks (partial overlap with prior ITSM background)

blocks.heading: Go straight here — skip ITIL 4
blocks.text: ITIL Foundation (Version 5) is the current edition; ITIL 4 and v5 are running in parallel during the transition, but v3 is not accepted as a prerequisite for upper-level v5 certifications regardless of which one you sit first, so there's no advantage to studying ITIL 4 now. This is a bigger jump from v3 than a "refresh," though — v5 moved the emphasis away from named practices (where your v3 depth used to count) toward the Service Value System and core terminology, and added entirely new territory: AI, framework alignment, and product/service lifecycle.

items.label: Four Dimensions of Product & Service Mgmt

items.text: Service Value System (SVS) in depth — guiding principles, governance, service value chain, continual improvement (now the dominant domain, was ~1 of many in v3/v4)
Core ITSM terminology: Service, Value, Cost, Utility, Warranty, Risk, Output vs Outcome
Four Dimensions Model (organizations & people, information & technology, partners & suppliers, value streams & processes)
Product and service lifecycle — planning through retirement (new in v5)
Value streams: flow-based thinking and mapping (new in v5)
ITIL and AI — AI as a supporting operational capability (new in v5)
ITIL's relationship to DevOps and PRINCE2 (new framing in v5)
Note: named practices (Incident, Problem, Change Enablement, Service Desk, etc.) are no longer individually tested at Foundation level — deprioritize deep practice study versus v4

blocks.heading: Resources
blocks.text: Official syllabus: search "ITIL Foundation Version 5 Candidate Syllabus" via peoplecert.org or axelos.com. Confirm current availability in your region — rollout has been phased.

year1.title: AI-200: Azure AI Cloud Developer Associate
year1.issuer: Microsoft — successor to the retired AZ-204

blocks.heading: Prerequisites Microsoft names explicitly
blocks.text: Azure SDKs (incl. Python), Azure data management services, Azure monitoring/troubleshooting, messaging & eventing, vector databases, and containerized applications on Azure. This is the exam where your Python push and your Docker practice both pay off directly.

items.label: AI solutions via Azure data management services
Connect to and consume Azure services

items.text: Build/store/version images with Azure Container Registry (ACR) + ACR Tasks
Deploy containers to Azure App Service (env vars, secrets)
Azure Container Apps — environments, revisions, KEDA event-driven scaling
Deploy/manage AKS workloads via manifest files; monitor & troubleshoot AKS
Cosmos DB for NoSQL — SDK queries, RU optimization, vector similarity search, change feed
Azure Database for PostgreSQL — SDK queries, schema/indexing, vector workloads, RAG patterns
Azure Managed Redis — caching/expiration/invalidation, vector indexing
Azure Service Bus — queue & process operations
Azure Event Grid — event-driven workflows
Azure Functions — triggers, bindings, serverless APIs, deployment
Azure Key Vault — secrets, rotation, retrieval
Azure App Configuration
OpenTelemetry SDKs for distributed tracing
KQL (Kusto Query Language) for logs & metrics

blocks.heading: Resources
blocks.text: Official study guide: learn.microsoft.com — AI-200 study guide. Free hands-on paths via Microsoft Learn modules for each service listed above.

year1.title: AI-103: Azure AI App and Agent Developer Associate
year1.issuer: Microsoft — successor to the retired AI-102

blocks.heading: Prerequisites Microsoft names explicitly
blocks.text: Experience building apps in Python, plus familiarity with general AI capabilities, generative AI concepts, and Azure services. Take this after AI-200 — it assumes the Azure app-development foundation and layers AI-specific building on top.

items.label: Implement generative AI and agentic solutions
Plan and manage an Azure AI solution

items.text: Choosing the right Azure AI Foundry services for a given generative AI/agent scenario
Setting up AI solutions in Foundry; managing, monitoring, securing AI systems
Responsible AI principles applied to generative and agentic systems
Build generative applications using Azure AI Foundry
Build agents in Foundry (orchestration, tools, grounding)
Optimize and operationalize generative AI systems in production
Image and video generation; multimodal understanding workflows
Language model text analysis; speech solutions
Retrieval & grounding pipelines (RAG); document content extraction

blocks.heading: Resources
blocks.text: Official study guide: learn.microsoft.com — AI-103 study guide.

blocks.heading: Ground this one before you sit it
blocks.text: Unlike the rest of this roadmap, you don't currently use Terraform anywhere — not at work, not freelance. A cert with no practice behind it is exactly the weak signal this whole plan has otherwise avoided. Fix: provision one real thing with it before or during study — the hosting for a freelance client project, or even a personal side project — so the credential is backed by something you actually did, not just a multiple-choice pass. No formal prerequisite otherwise, and the exam is knowledge-based rather than hands-on like CKA. Your Nintex/UiPath instinct — defining a desired end-state and letting a tool reconcile it — is conceptually the same idea Terraform applies to infrastructure, so the mental model will feel familiar even though the syntax (HCL) is new.

items.text: Infrastructure as Code with Terraform — concepts, advantages, multi-cloud capability
Terraform fundamentals — installing/using providers, provider role, managing state
Core workflow — init, validate, plan, apply, destroy, fmt
Configuration — resources, data sources, variables, outputs, complex types, expressions, functions, custom validation
Modules — sourcing, variable scope, versioning
State management — local/remote backends, state locking, drift
Infrastructure maintenance — importing existing infra, inspecting state via CLI, verbose logging
HCP Terraform — workspaces/projects, collaboration features, integrations

blocks.heading: Resources
blocks.text: Official exam content list: developer.hashicorp.com — Terraform Associate 004 review. Confirm current exam fee at registration — HashiCorp/IBM pricing has shifted before.

blocks.heading: Why this comes last, and why Troubleshooting is your edge
blocks.text: This is the stretch goal for a reason — it's purely practical, no multiple choice, and requires real lab time. The single largest domain is Troubleshooting (30%), which plays directly to fifteen years of Tier 1/Tier 2 support and root-cause work — that instinct transfers, the syntax is what's new.

items.text: Cluster: kubeadm setup, RBAC, etcd backup & restore, node maintenance
Workloads: Pods, Deployments, ReplicaSets, DaemonSets, scheduling & scaling
Networking: Services (ClusterIP/NodePort/LoadBalancer), Ingress, Gateway API, NetworkPolicy
Storage: PersistentVolumes, PersistentVolumeClaims, StorageClasses
Troubleshooting: cluster, node, application, and networking failure diagnosis via kubectl/logs

blocks.heading: Resources
blocks.text: Official curriculum & candidate handbook: cncf.io — CKA. Practice exams via killer.sh (bundled with registration) are the closest simulation of the real exam's difficulty.

year2Intro.heading: Year 2+ — Conditional & optional
year2Intro.text: These four are real, respected credentials — not padding — but each is a bet tied to a specific direction rather than a default next move. Pursue one only once its trigger condition is actually true for you; otherwise the core five above is the complete, coherent plan.

year2plus.title: OSCP (OffSec Certified Professional)
year2plus.issuer: OffSec — the credible security credential, not CEH
year2plus.trigger: pursue only if application/security work becomes a dedicated direction beyond the Postgraduate Diploma's Information Security and Ethical Hacking modules. This is a 3+ month, full-time-equivalent commitment — not a side credential, and not a substitute for CEH, which stays off this roadmap entirely regardless of tier.

items.text: Enumeration methodology — systematic reconnaissance before exploitation
Web application exploitation fundamentals
Linux and Windows privilege escalation techniques
Active Directory attack chains — kerberoasting, lateral movement, domain admin paths
Buffer overflow basics
Professional report writing — the exam is graded on documentation, not just access

year2plus.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate (SAA-C03)
year2plus.trigger: pursue only if you want reach beyond Microsoft-stack-aligned companies, or a specific opportunity is explicitly AWS-native. You've already committed to Azure via AI-200/AI-103 — don't duplicate cloud fundamentals for the sake of a second logo unless there's a real reason.

items.text: IAM policies, roles, and least-privilege design
VPC networking, security groups, subnetting
S3 storage classes and lifecycle policies
EC2, Auto Scaling, and Elastic Load Balancing
RDS and DynamoDB — when to use which
Multi-AZ and disaster-recovery design patterns
Caching with CloudFront and ElastiCache
Cost optimization — Reserved Instances, Spot, Savings Plans
AWS Well-Architected Framework pillars

year2plus.title: Certified Kubernetes Application Developer (CKAD)
year2plus.trigger: pursue only if more of your target work leans app-development-on-Kubernetes rather than cluster operations. Significant overlap with CKA — treat this as an add-on once CKA is done, never a substitute for it.

items.text: Multi-container Pod patterns (sidecar, init containers)
Helm and Kustomize for deployment management
Health checks and readiness/liveness probes
ConfigMaps, Secrets, ServiceAccounts, SecurityContexts
Resource requests and limits
Debugging running workloads via logs and exec

year2plus.title: HashiCorp Certified: Vault Associate (003)
year2plus.trigger: the natural pairing if both the security direction and Terraform land for real — secrets management sits exactly at that intersection. Skip if neither becomes an actual focus; don't collect it just because it exists.

items.text: Authentication methods (AppRole, LDAP, and others)
Policy-as-code for access control
Token lifecycle and management
Dynamic secrets and lease renewal/revocation
Secrets engines — KV, database, cloud provider engines
Encryption as a Service (the Transit engine)
Vault architecture — storage backends, high availability
Deployment topology and access management integration

footer: Built from official Microsoft Learn, HashiCorp, CNCF, OffSec, AWS, and PeopleCert/AXELOS sources, August 2026. Exam formats, weightings, and pricing change — reconfirm against the official source before registering, especially for AI-200/AI-103/ITIL v5 given how new they are.
